heading: Two pointers, one job
body: One pointer scans the array, the other tracks where to **place** the next non-zero. Swap when you find a non-zero, increment the placement pointer. Zeros naturally slide to the end — no extra pass needed.

heading: Why swap beats assignment
body: Swapping kills two birds with one stone: non-zeros move forward **and** zeros move back in the same operation. If you just assigned forward, you'd need a second loop to fill the tail with zeros.

label: Crux · Python

q: Why do we swap elements instead of just assigning non-zero values forward?
options: Swapping is faster than assignment in Python
Swapping ensures zeros naturally move to the end without extra logic
Assignment would require tracking zero positions separately

explain: Swapping moves non-zero elements forward while pushing zeros backward — no extra logic needed to fill the tail.
